steps.title: One-Way Valve Removal

items.text: Guano, urine, and oils produce a strong, musty odor that spreads through the home.

items.title: Colonies grow fast

inspect.h2: Assessing Raccoon Activity in Your Attic
inspect.p: We take a close look at your attic and property to assess raccoon activity, identify possible entry points, and review any visible damage. Sounds alone don't confirm raccoons, so an inspection helps determine the animal involved and the options for your property.
items: Assessment of attic activity and signs of raccoon presence
Review of possible entry points around the roof and structure
Inspection of visible damage near vents, soffits, and openings
Check for dependent young before any sealing is considered

images.alt: Close-up of raccoon safely secured in humane trap
Two raccoons safely contained in a humane trap during removal

signs.h2: Signs You May Have a Raccoon
signs.p: These signs can point to raccoon activity, but an inspection helps confirm the animal — since sounds alone don't confirm raccoons.

items.text: Heavy movement or thumping in the attic at night
Disturbed, matted, or displaced insulation
Visible damage near roof vents, soffits, or openings
Torn screens, chewed fascia, or pulled-back vents

solution.p: Removal and exclusion are assessed as options for your property based on what the inspection finds.

steps.title: Assessment
steps.text: We assess the attic for raccoon activity, identify possible entry points, and review visible damage to understand what's happening on the property.

steps.title: Removal Options
steps.text: Removal is approached based on the animal and situation found. We check for dependent young before any removal or sealing is planned.

steps.title: Exclusion Options
steps.text: Sealing entry points is considered only after animals and any dependent young are confirmed out, helping reduce the chance of re-entry.

why.p: Sounds in the attic can come from several animals. An inspection helps identify the animal and the right next steps.

items.title: Sounds aren't conclusive
items.text: Raccoons, squirrels, rats, and opossums can all make noise in an attic. An inspection helps identify the actual animal.

items.title: Check for dependent young
items.text: Before sealing any entry points, it's important to confirm no dependent young are left inside the structure.

items.title: Entry points vary
items.text: Roof vents, soffits, and gaps near the roofline are common access points. An inspection locates the specific openings.

faq.p: Common questions about suspected raccoons and how removal is assessed.

items.question: How do I know if it's a raccoon in my attic?
items.answer: Sounds alone don't confirm raccoons — squirrels, rats, and opossums can make similar noise. An on-site inspection helps identify the animal responsible based on entry points, tracks, droppings, and the type of damage present.

items.question: How is raccoon removal assessed?
items.answer: We assess the attic for activity, locate possible entry points, and review visible damage. Removal and exclusion are then recommended as options for the property based on what we find during the inspection.

items.question: What does raccoon removal cost?
items.answer: Cost depends on the inspection findings and the scope of the work involved. After the assessment, we can walk you through the options and any associated pricing before anything is done.

items.question: How do you prevent raccoons from coming back?
items.answer: Exclusion focuses on sealing entry points — but only after confirming the animals and any dependent young are out. Sealing too early can trap young inside, so checking for babies is an important step before any repairs are made.
